ὑπεμνήμῡκε , in Il. 22.491 , πάντα δ᾽ ὑπεμνήμυκε, of an orphan boy: Aristarch. interpreted it—
A.he hangs down his head utterly, he is altogether cast down; so that it must be taken (cf. Sch.) as Ep.
pf. of ὑπ-ημύω, for ὑπ-εμήμυκε (ν being inserted metri gr.):—the pres. is used by coluth. 338 , ὑπημύουσι παρειαί sink in, become hollow.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
